text:
[
  {
    "n": 1,
    "title": "Defining Artificial Intelligence: The Russell-Norvig Matrix and System Scope",
    "scope": "Establishes the core theoretical definitions of AI based on the 2x2 matrix categorised by reasoning versus behaviour and human fidelity versus rationality. Distinguishes between Weak (Narrow) AI and Strong AI (Artificial General Intelligence). Explores the scope of intelligence simulation versus human-based cognitive construction.",
    "key_points": [
      "Four definition quadrants: Thinking Humanly (cognitive modelling), Thinking Rationally (laws of thought/logic), Acting Humanly (Turing test approach), and Acting Rationally (rational agent approach)",
      "Rational agent definition: an entity that acts to achieve the best expected outcome given available information",
      "Weak AI: domain-specific intelligence simulation and task-focused problem solving (dominates contemporary AI development)",
      "Strong AI (AGI): general human-level cognitive architecture capable of transferring knowledge across arbitrary domains"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 2,
    "title": "Core AI Subfields and the Turing Test Framework",
    "scope": "Details the six foundational disciplines required to achieve comprehensive artificial intelligence according to Russell and Norvig. Differentiates the Standard Turing Test from the Full Turing Test in terms of input modalities and physical grounding.",
    "key_points": [
      "Six core subfields: Natural Language Processing (NLP), Knowledge Representation, Automated Reasoning, Machine Learning, Computer Vision, and Robotics",
      "Standard Turing Test: operational benchmark testing blind linguistic communication, requiring NLP, Knowledge Representation, Automated Reasoning, and Machine Learning",
      "Full Turing Test: extends evaluation to physical interactions with the world, adding Computer Vision (perceiving objects) and Robotics (manipulating objects and physical navigation)"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 3,
    "title": "Biomimetic, Swarm, and Embodied Intelligence",
    "scope": "Examines non-human intelligences used as architectural models for artificial systems. Covers biological inspiration including swarm intelligence, evolutionary processes, and the theoretical distinction between disembodied software agents and embodied physical systems.",
    "key_points": [
      "Biomimicry and bioinspired systems: porting natural functional mechanisms to artificial computational designs (e.g., biological sonar to synthetic sensing)",
      "Swarm intelligence: emergent collective coordination arising from decentralized, simple agents (bird flocking, ant colony food foraging, bee flower-scouting algorithms)",
      "Evolutionary computation: search and optimization methods inspired by natural selection, genetics, and selective breeding",
      "Embodied AI: physical embodiment (robots interacting with physical constraints) versus digital embodiment (software agents like virtual assistants or video game NPCs)"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 4,
    "title": "Situational Intelligence and Cognitive Offloading",
    "scope": "Analyzes how intelligence is situated in cultural and operational contexts rather than existing as an absolute scale. Models the progressive offloading of perceptual, cognitive, and physical human skills into technological systems, using the multi-stage evolution of driving automation as a primary case.",
    "key_points": [
      "Situational dependency: survival skills, botanical knowledge, and navigation in indigenous tribes versus technical literacy in urban environments",
      "Cognitive and physical offloading: the transition of once-essential survival capabilities into niche, domain-specific hobbies (e.g., equestrian husbandry replaced by automotive transport)",
      "Gradual automotive automation progression: power steering, clutch assists, automatic transmissions, ABS, electronic stability control, backup cameras, drive-by-wire, to autonomous driving",
      "Edge-case management: human off-board teleoperation teams maintaining supervisory control over unresolved autonomous vehicle scenarios"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 5,
    "title": "Technological Paradigms: The Four Industrial Revolutions",
    "scope": "Traces the structural shifts in production across economic history from the First through the Fourth Industrial Revolutions. Clarifies the qualitative leap of Industry 4.0 from physical muscle automation to cognitive work participation.",
    "key_points": [
      "First Industrial Revolution (1760–1840): steam power, textile machinery, and early mechanical manufacturing",
      "Second Industrial Revolution (1870–1914): electrification, chemical synthesis, assembly lines, and mass industrial production",
      "Third Industrial Revolution (1970–2000): microelectronics, digital computing, initial office automation, and programmable robotics",
      "Fourth Industrial Revolution (2010–present): convergence of AI, IoT, cyber-physical systems, autonomous robotics, cloud infrastructure, and advanced connectivity",
      "Cognitive expansion: transition from automating physical kinetic energy to automating cognitive labour (language generation, data analysis, decision support, and creative synthesis)"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 6,
    "title": "The Task-Based Labour Framework and Computerisation Bottlenecks",
    "scope": "Presents modern labour economics theory viewing occupations as bundles of tasks rather than monolithic roles. Deconstructs the 2x2 routine/cognitive automation matrix and examines the empirical bottlenecks identified by Frey and Osborne.",
    "key_points": [
      "Task-based occupation model: jobs consist of distinct functional sub-tasks (e.g., a teacher lecturing, preparing syllabi, grading, and counselling)",
      "Routine vs Non-routine x Manual vs Cognitive matrix: traditional machines automated routine manual (assembly) and routine cognitive (data entry); AI penetrates non-routine cognitive tasks, while non-routine manual (plumbing, physical care) remains resistant",
      "Frey and Osborne (2013/2017) baseline: 47% of US jobs assessed as susceptible to computerisation over 10–20 years based on task attributes",
      "The Three Engineering Bottlenecks: Perception and Manipulation (unstructured environments), Creative Intelligence (original ideation), and Social Intelligence (negotiation, empathy, persuasion)",
      "Generative AI reappraisal (2024): core engineering bottlenecks remain durable despite advancements in syntactic fluency"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 7,
    "title": "Labour Market Dynamics: Substitution, Complementarity, and Firm Expansion",
    "scope": "Contrasts the economic mechanics of automation: direct labour substitution versus worker complementarity. Explores empirical labour market outcomes including firm-level productivity gains, junior versus senior developer polarization, and demographic vulnerabilities.",
    "key_points": [
      "Substitution vs Complementarity: substitution replaces human effort with capital; complementarity enhances worker productivity, quality, or safety, driving up labour value",
      "Firm expansion effects: AI integration can raise firm-level productivity, allowing geographic and product expansion that increases net employment (e.g., observed 15% job growth in adopting firms)",
      "Labour market polarisation: disproportionate vulnerability of consumer-facing, retail, and gig roles occupied by younger workers",
      "IT industry restructuring: declining demand for junior developers whose routine coding tasks are automated, shifting hiring premiums entirely to middle and senior engineers"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 8,
    "title": "Generative AI Constraints, Institutional Lags, and Multi-Stakeholder Adaptation",
    "scope": "Evaluates the inherent system vulnerabilities of generative models and the socio-technical lag between technological capability and institutional readiness. Outlines structural adaptation policies required across governments, universities, enterprises, and individual professionals.",
    "key_points": [
      "Generative AI limitations: confident confabulation/hallucination, historical data bias, lack of accountability, absent physical grounding, and essential requirement for human verification",
      "Socio-technical lag: organizational, legal, and institutional adaptation consistently moves slower than software capability deployment",
      "Multi-level adaptation matrix: government safety nets and training infrastructure, higher education focus on critical evaluation over rote generation, corporate gradual rollout with workforce retraining",
      "High-value human competencies: complex problem-solving, ethical judgment, critical thinking, domain-specific deep expertise, emotional intelligence, and AI literacy"
    ]
  }
]
